text:
ZigZag

 Visit zigzag.diy · Download for
Mac,
Windows or
Linux

ZigZag is a visual embroidery editor built in Rust for performance, with
built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) support so AI agents can create and
edit designs alongside you. Turn SVG artwork into stitches, fine-tune it in
the editor, and export PES, DST, EXP, JEF, or VP3 for broad compatibility
with embroidery machines—or send designs directly to a Brother Skitch
(PP1) over Bluetooth .

Draw in Illustrator, draw in ZigZag, or let an agent draw. The Rust engine
and zigzag command-line tool power the same workflow outside the editor.

 See ZigZag in action

 

 Stitching on a Brother Skitch (PP1)

 Download for Windows

 Download ZigZag for Windows 
— the ZigZag- -x86 64-windows-setup.exe asset on the latest release.

For 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1709 or later) and Windows 11. Run the
installer: it needs no administrator rights, adds ZigZag to the Start menu
and to Open with for SVG and stitch files, and can put zigzag-cli on the
PATH. Uninstall it from Settings › Apps. The
 ZigZag- -x86 64-windows.zip asset holds the same files without an
installer: unzip it and double-click ZigZag.exe . Windows SmartScreen may
warn the first time a download runs; click More info → Run anyway . No
Rust installation is needed.

 Download for Linux

 Download ZigZag for Linux 
— the ZigZag- -x86 64-linux.tar.gz asset on the latest release.

For x86-64 Linux desktops with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+),
X11 or Wayland, and OpenGL. Extract the archive and run ./zigzag-studio 
inside the extracted folder. It also includes the zigzag CLI and
 zigzag-mcp bridge; no Rust installation is needed. See the included
 README.txt for runtime dependencies and Bluetooth setup.

Release notes and checksums
· Changelog
· Publishing a release

 Privacy

ZigZag works without an account, sends no usage statistics or crash reports,
and keeps your designs on your computer unless you share them. It asks GitHub
whether there's a newer release (Settings › General turns that off) and talks
to zigzag.diy only when you sign in, sync or share a design. The details are
in the privacy policy.

 Code signing policy

- Mac: releases are signed with the maintainer's Apple Developer ID and
 notarized by Apple.
- Windows: the installer and the three executables are signed in the
 maintainer's name, verified by Microsoft
 (Azure Artifact Signing).
 Releases up to 0.1.11 were unsigned.

Windows releases are built and signed on GitHub Actions from the tagged
source (windows-release.yml), and
the run fails if any of those files comes out without a valid signature.
Nothing built anywhere else is signed.

 Build

 

Linux needs the usual X11/Wayland and OpenGL dev libraries for gui . libdbus
is vendored for ble .

 Development

 

Run the studio's tests with cargo test --features gui (plain cargo test 
skips them).

- Letter census: tools/census/census.sh NAME sets every letter and digit of about 50 popular fonts of every kind of type ( tools/census/fonts.txt ) as a satin and counts how many come out clean on every measure (no filled parts, stitches off the letter, extra cuts, travel in sight, bare cloth, off-square stitches, seams or satin piled three deep), with trims and letters sewn in one piece. It takes about half a minute; quick sweeps every 8th installed family and full all of them. Each process is stopped past 2 GB. ZIGZAG FONT SIZE=11 sets letters about 8 mm tall. tools/census/summary.py compares runs in target/census/ . To try a change, tools/census/try.sh [VAR=VALUE …] runs the popular fonts at 8 and 15 mm as sewn and with the settings given, in one go, and shows each against the last try (results for code that hasn't changed are kept). tools/census/letter.sh FAMILY CHAR [8 15] [VAR=VALUE …] plans one letter and says where each trim is and why ( ZIGZAG TRIMS=1 does that for any zigzag convert ); tools/census/trims.py sorts a census's trims that way, for a census run with ZIGZAG TRIMS=1 . tools/census/sheet.py OUT.png [8 15] FAMILY=CHARS … draws letters' stitches in a few settings side by side over their outlines, to judge by eye; tools/census/judged.txt is a set judged that way and tools/census/judge.py checks the census's faults against it (the census counts stitches crowded into one place, the narrow end of a fan, and needle points outside the letter, but judges fans poorly). They build with the trial profile: as fast as release, but an edit rebuilds in seconds.

- App icons: the embroidered icons live in packaging/macos/AppIcon.png 
 (light) and packaging/macos/AppIcon-dark.png (dark). The Mac build
 regenerates both .icns files; bash packaging/macos/make-icons.sh does it
 separately. Finder and the unopened app use the light icon; while the studio
 runs, its Dock icon follows the app's theme.
- Screenshots and videos: start the studio with ZIGZAG CAPTURE= 
 and ⌃⌥⌘S saves the window as a full-resolution PNG; ⌃⌥⌘R starts and stops
 recording it. packaging/media/encode.sh /take-001 demo turns a
 recording into demo.mp4 and demo.gif (needs ffmpeg).

install.title: Download for Mac
install.html:
Download ZigZag.dmg

For Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, macOS 11 or later. Open the DMG, then drag ZigZag into Applications. The release is signed and notarized by Apple. No Rust installation is needed.

Or with Homebrew:

brew install --cask simpsoka/zigzag/zigzag

To update a Homebrew installation:

brew upgrade --cask --greedy simpsoka/zigzag/zigzag

ZigZag also updates itself: it tells you when there's a newer release and installs it when you say (ZigZag › Check for Updates…).
